newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP drops demand for TV quotas.
newsitem.headline: EP drops demand for TV quotas.

text.p: The European Parliament abandoned on Tuesday its long-standing demands for stricter limits on the number of Hollywood programmes on European television, sidestepping a showdown with EU capitals.

Although a majority of deputies demanded that a rule that 51 percent of Europe's screentime should be devoted to European works be made mandatory, the proposal failed to secure the qualified majority needed to force EU governments to negotiate on the issue.

The vote brings to an end one of the EU's longest-running sagas, surrounding the EU's 1989 television without frontiers directive which deputies had hoped to use to brake Hollywood's domination of the EU's television screens.

"Very powerful interests have won today," British Socialist deputy Carole Tongue, a member of the parliament's Culture Committee, told Reuters, pointing to the United States' $6 billion trade surplus with the EU in the audiovisual sector.
The parliament had effectively been fighting a losing battle with EU culture ministers who had made clear in advance they had no intention of curbing the prime U.S. export industry.
But it stuck by two other key demands.

It will press in talks with EU governments demands for all new television sets to be equipped within a year with a so-called V-chip, which would allow parents to screen out violent programmes from their children.
A spokesman for Culture Commissioner Marcelino Oreja said the demand was unrealistic as the technology would not be available in time.
It will press for rules to ensure that pay-television does not prevent ordinary viewers from watching major soccer events like the World Cup.
